summary: A way of splitting up the people, places or things your work is about, so you can compare the parts: by region, by depot, by product line.
example: Region: members are split by the growing region they farm in, so regions can be compared.
definition: A segment is a slice of what the organisation serves or works across, used to compare one part with another: a finding in one region against another, a measure in one depot against another. First define the slicing itself, as a segment with no parent (Region), then each slice under it (Northern region). A gap names the slices its evidence covers, a piece of work says which of those it reaches, and a KPI is broken down by the same slicing, so a finding and its measure always cut the work the same way. A segment describes where or what, never who does the work: it is not a resource (a role, unit, partner, system or place the work draws on, such as a Depot supervisor), not a beneficiary group (the people the work is for, such as Depot staff), not a team (who carries the work), not a label (a free tag nobody planned), and not a period of time (that is a reporting cycle). The test: if you would count or compare a measure across it, it is a segment; if it does something, decides something or is paid for, it is not.

/spec/parent.guide: The slicing this is one slice of (Region, for the northern region), or the broader slice it sits inside. Leave it empty for the slicing itself. A segment can never sit under itself, directly or further up, and such a parent is refused on save. When the slicing does not exist yet, define it first.

poor.why: A team, not a segment: the parent is the dimension the slice belongs to, here Depot.

/spec/description.guide: What falls inside this slice and what does not, precisely enough that two people counting it would agree, including how a borderline case is counted.
good: Which collection depot produce passed through. Every depot in the network is a value; produce collected in the field is counted against the depot it was taken to.
Which line produce belongs to. A crate is counted against one line only, by what it mostly holds.

poor.why: Does not say where a region's boundary comes from, so two people could count a holding differently.
Says why it matters, not what falls inside it.

/metadata/name.guide: The slicing (Region, Product line) or one slice of it (Northern region, Fresh produce), as people say it.

poor.why: A role, which is a resource: it does work. A segment is a slice you compare a measure across, such as the depot itself.
The people the work is for, which is a beneficiary group. Slice by where they work (Depot) if you need to compare.
Who carries the work, which is a team.
A period of time, which a reporting cycle holds.
A free label, not a planned way of slicing what you serve.

Gap:/spec/segments.ask: Which gaps were observed in this slice? Each gap lists the segments its evidence covers.
Gap:/spec/segments.ifNone: Nothing has to be defined first: a segment may be declared before any gap names it. When a gap's evidence covers this slice, name the segment on the gap.

KPI:/spec/disaggregations.ask: Which KPIs are broken down by this dimension? Each KPI lists the dimensions it is split by.
KPI:/spec/disaggregations.ifNone: Leave it: only a dimension, a segment with no parent, is a disaggregation, and a KPI names it when its source can report the split.
